name: sorted()
what_it_does: Returns a NEW list with the items of an iterable arranged in order, without changing the original.
parameters: iterable - what to sort. key (optional) - a function applied to each item to decide sort order. reverse (optional) - True for descending order.
return_value: A new, sorted list. The original iterable is never modified.
common_mistakes: Confusing sorted(x) (returns a new list, x unchanged) with x.sort() (sorts a list in place, returns None) - assigning `x = x.sort()` is a classic bug that sets x to None. Sorting a list with mixed incompatible types raises TypeError.
when_to_use: Whenever you need an ordered version of some data without disturbing the original order elsewhere in your program.
